title: MV self switch parallel process (Chrono Engine)

posts.author: stprod
posts.body:
Good day.
I'm using the
Chrono Engine
plugin for
RPG Maker MV
(real-time battle).
I've already set everything up. Everything works great.
I'm having a problem using self-switches for enemies.
I set up self-switch C (notetag on database) so that when an enemy dies, a new event page with its death sprite is displayed.
The problem is that I want that new event page to be in a parallel process to switch to two more graphics (death animation), but nothing ever happens. It's as if the event remains completely inactive (even though it's in a parallel process).  It also doesn't work to put all those instructions in the movement routes of that event page.
Is there any way to fix this?
Thanks.

It might be - I don't know that plugin, never having used it.
But such a possibility doesn't really make sense to me, because nothing on that event page tells the engine that it is an enemy event, and other event pages are not processed. That's why I considered but dismissed that possibility before my first post.
But I admit, my focus was on checking if you had an error in the page priority or something like that.
I suppose you now have to wait for the answer of someone who uses that plugin.

posts.author: Slaughty
posts.body:
If I'm not mistaken, when a battler dies in chrono engine, the event is erased similar to the event erase command. So any of the event commands following its death never run because the event is erased. Using the death self switch is more for when the map is re-entered/reloaded to not have the enemy "respawn".
Hope this helps, good luck.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
The OP's notetag is not wrong. That's what it looks like in Chrono Engine. Since OP said the page does execute entering the map again, the self switch is being toggled, but it happened after the enemy died, and the OP commenting out that line of code doesn't stop it from dying.
When an enemy dies ChronoEngine automatically drops its opacity to 0 then erases the event.
